aois.name: Port Said / Suez North Anchorage
aois.notes: Reference AOI (reliable: median tile cloud 9%, ~3-day median gap). Two tiles overlap the search bbox (T36RVV + T36SVA); T36SVA starts at 31.54N and does NOT cover the anchorage core - footprint-coverage filtering on core_bbox is mandatory. Full AOI north of 31.64N would need a two-tile mosaic; the core crop sits inside T36RVV.

aois.name: Singapore Anchorage
aois.notes: Countable (>100 vessels visible in a clear scene) but weather-gated: median tile cloud 53%, only 1 of 23 passes in 90 days was <20% tile cloud. Tile cloud overstates anchorage cloud - AOI-level SCL screening is the mitigation. Core is the Eastern Anchorage / Singapore Strait off Changi.

aois.name: Rotterdam / Europoort Anchorage
aois.notes: Anchorage areas off Hoek van Holland / Maasvlakte plus Europoort approaches. Temperate maritime cloud - expect a usable pair most windows, not every window.

aois.name: Shanghai / Yangshan Anchorage
aois.notes: AOI is the Yangshan deep-water port + offshore anchorage (graph node sea_shanghai at 31.23,121.48 is the Waigaoqiao side; Yangshan at ~30.62,122.07 is the countable anchorage). Dense traffic; haze/fog can mimic cloud in SCL screening.

aois.name: Busan Anchorage
aois.notes: Southern anchorage off Busan New Port / Gadeokdo. Monsoon-season cloud is the main gate. Core sits wholly inside MGRS tile 52SED: the natural anchorage box straddles the 129.0E tile seam (52SDD/52SED) and no single tile covered a wider core, so the core sits on the 52SED side of the seam.

aois.name: Jebel Ali Anchorage
aois.notes: Offshore anchorage NW of Jebel Ali port. Arid climate - Port Said-like reliability expected; dust haze is the residual risk (SCL may class it unclassified, not cloud). Core is the compact port/anchorage box inside the overlap of tiles 40RBN/40RCN granules: a wider core straddles the ~54.9-55.0E seam and no single tile covers it.

aois.name: Strait of Gibraltar / Algeciras Bay Anchorage
aois.notes: Graph node is the chokepoint (chk_gibraltar); the countable anchorage is in Algeciras Bay + the eastern strait waiting areas. Bunkering queues are the congestion signal here.

aois.name: Panama Canal Anchorages (Balboa / Cristobal)
aois.notes: Search bbox spans both canal entrances; core_bbox is the Balboa (Pacific) anchorage, the larger waiting area. Cristobal (Atlantic) anchorage is inside the search bbox but outside the core - a scene covering only Cristobal is rejected by the coverage filter, by design. Tropical cloud like Singapore.

aois.name: Los Angeles / San Pedro Bay Anchorage (West)
aois.notes: Western San Pedro Bay anchorage areas. Overlaps the Long Beach AOI (shared bay, distinct anchorage areas) - counts for the two nodes are not additive. Marine layer (low stratus) is the classic false-clear risk.

aois.name: Long Beach / San Pedro Bay Anchorage (East)
aois.notes: Eastern San Pedro Bay anchorage areas off Long Beach / Seal Beach. See the Los Angeles AOI note on overlap - do not sum the two counts.

aois.name: Hamburg / Elbe Anchorage
aois.notes: River port: vessels sit at berth along the Elbe rather than in an open anchorage, so counts read berth occupancy more than queue length. The downstream waiting anchorage near the Elbe mouth is outside economical single-scene framing. Northern-European cloud applies.

aois.name: Antwerp / Scheldt Anchorage
aois.notes: Scheldt river anchorages + Deurganckdok approaches. Like Hamburg, partly a berth-occupancy read.

aois.name: Santos Anchorage
aois.notes: Offshore anchorage off Santos / Sao Paulo coast. Southern-hemisphere winter (Jun-Aug) is the clearer season.

aois.name: New York / Ambrose Anchorage
aois.notes: Ambrose anchorage + Lower Bay waiting areas offshore of the graph node's harbour position. Winter storms and summer haze both gate usability.

aois.name: Malacca Strait Anchorage (off Port Klang)
aois.notes: Graph node is the chokepoint (chk_malacca); the countable anchorage is the strait waiting area off Port Klang. Same tropical cloud regime as Singapore - expect SCL screening to matter and usable pairs to be scarce in wet months.

comment: Satellite Watch area-of-interest registry. node_id values are graph ids from data/graph/graph.json. bbox = STAC search box [min_lon, min_lat, max_lon, max_lat]. core_bbox = the anchorage crop that a single Sentinel-2 tile footprint MUST fully cover before the scene is eligible (a tile that merely intersects the search bbox may miss the anchorage entirely, as at Port Said). All imagery is Sentinel-2 L2A at 10 m/px; the countable class is large vessels >= ~150 m LOA only.
